subject: Re: Performance SLOs & context window impact  follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Performance SLOs & context window impact  follow-up and next steps

Hi Alex 

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on FinCo's performance requirements and how context window / token limits will affect latency: 

Summary of requirements you shared:
- P95 tail latency target: <= 300ms for single-turn API calls (no streaming) at expected median payloads.
- Streaming: some product paths require server-side streaming with sub-200ms first-byte time for short prompts.
- Typical input size: 1.5k tokens (user history + doc context); expected output: 150-300 tokens.
- Concurrency: bursts up to 250 concurrent users during peak; sustained baseline ~50 concurrent.
- Throughput target: ~3k generated tokens/sec aggregated across users.
- Security/compliance: customer data must be isolated (dedicated capacity considered).

Key technical notes (high level):
- Context window impacts per-request compute and KV cache behavior. Large inputs (1.5k tokens) increase per-token decode time and memory working set; we often see a ~10-30% latency uplift vs 512-token inputs depending on model/quantization.
- Streaming lowers perceived latency but can increase overhead (more small writes) if not using a streaming-optimized path.
- For your concurrency/throughput profile, Dedicated capacity with autoscaling + prefix caching for repeated contexts will reduce cost and help keep tail latencies stable.

Attachments: I attached the SLO worksheet you asked for and our performance playbook so you can see recommended GPU sizing and benchmarking methodology.

Next steps / asks from FinCo:
1) Can you confirm the 1.5k token typical input and whether that includes embeddings/doc chunks?
2) Are the streaming flows latency-sensitive on first-byte only, or do you need ordered low-latency token-by-token delivery?
3) Procurement contact (we'll need to loop in for contract redlines).

We'll pull together a short performance proposal (GPU sizing + expected p50/p95 numbers) and a canary plan for a Dedicated deployment. Rishi and Logan  can you validate the sizing assumptions below and propose a config we can present?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa  quick answers below: 

1) The 1.5k token figure is accurate for our user-facing assistant flows (includes doc chunks indexed into the prompt). For search/rerank paths it's much smaller (~200-400 tokens).
2) Streaming: for our chat UI we need progressive token delivery (ordered). First-byte latency target is important, but we also need smooth token delivery for real-time feel  sub-50ms inter-token for short outputs would be ideal, but we can relax that if overall responsiveness meets user expectations.
3) Procurement: procurement@finco.com (cc'd)  they'll need a preliminary cost/commit estimate.

Also: is there a recommended max input token you would suggest to keep p95 under 300ms, given your curated model catalog?

Alex

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & context window impact  follow-up and next steps

Alex  great, thanks for the clarifications. Attached is a short note on tradeoffs plus a proposed canary plan. High-level guidance from our catalog: 
- For strict p95 <= 300ms (non-streaming) we recommend targeting <= 1k input tokens for our latency-optimized model variants at x1 quantization; beyond that you should expect latency to grow roughly linearly with input tokens due to attention compute and KV population costs.
- If you need full 1.5k inputs, we can meet that at p95 with Dedicated capacity on the recommended GPU profile (see attached), but cost and reserved capacity commitments increase.
- For streaming ordered token delivery, we recommend the streaming-optimized runtime (reduces first-byte by offloading small-batch decode paths). That typically meets sub-200ms first-byte for common prompts and can sustain low inter-token spacing if configured with minimal batching on decode.

I've added two action items for Procurement to start a region/commit sizing conversation so we can get a Dedicated quote. Rishi/Logan  any changes to the technical guidance before I send an executive summary to Alex and Procurement?

Best,
Marissa

Team  internal note: Alex wants firm guidance for 1.5k token inputs with p95 <= 300ms and ordered streaming for chat. Initial thoughts:
- If we avoid heavy batching on decode and use streaming-optimized path, first-byte should be fine, but sustained token throughput may need dedicated quota.
- Need concrete GPU count (N) for canary that demonstrates both 1.5k input p95 and ordered streaming under 50 concurrent streams.

Please reply with the canary config (gpu type, instance count, memory + kv cache sizing) and any recommended runtime flags (quantization profile, batch limits, streaming buffer sizes).

Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: FinCo follow-up  sizing & streaming question

Marissa / Logan  quick technical reply for the canary proposal: 

Proposed canary config (conservative):
- GPU: 4x A800 / equivalent (8x for heavy redundancy if you want headroom).
- Model variant: latency-optimized quantized 4-bit profile (we've validated on similar workloads).
- Expected performance: for 1.5k input + 200 token output, p50 ~ 140-180ms, p95 ~ 220-320ms depending on background load and whether streaming batching triggers.
- Streaming: set decode_batch_max = 1 for paths that require ordered low-latency token delivery; enable streaming-optimized kernel path. That yields sub-200ms first-byte in our tests and inter-token spacing ~30-80ms depending on token size.
- Concurrency/throughput: with 4 GPUs we expect to sustain ~60-80 concurrent streaming sessions with the above profile; to hit FinCo's peak burst (250) we'd recommend autoscaling to 12 GPUs or suggest a hybrid: dedicated baseline + burst on hosted region.

Risks/notes:
- Large persistent context (1.5k tokens) increases memory and KV cache pressure; make sure cache eviction policy retains hot prefixes.
- If they insist on strict p95 <= 300ms at 250 concurrent users, pricing will reflect required reserved capacity.

I'll prepare a short slide with measured p50/p95 numbers from our bench and the playbook snippets. Happy to join the next call.

-Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
